title: Salt and Spire Again
premise: Ines Oyelaran, last apprentice of the Salt Road Guides' Guild, smuggles goods and secrets through the Thornfell mountains while the guild's numbers dwindle and the Crown's new Wardens close the old paths. When a mute child arrives at the guildhouse speaking Vessarine—the tongue of a kingdom erased from maps two centuries ago—Ines realizes the girl is a living key to the Hollow Door, the gate through which Vessar was sealed away. Hunted by Warden-Captain Aldric Vane, who wants the Door destroyed forever, and aided by her found family of outcasts—a disgraced cartographer, an ex-Warden deserter, and the guild's stubborn matriarch—Ines must retrace her dead mentor's final route. At the Door she learns the child is Vessar's last heir, offered a choice: reopen the kingdom and unleash what was imprisoned with it, or seal it and let Vessar die truly. Ines chooses a third path—she takes the heir's place as the Door's living anchor, trading her freedom for the child's future, and returns changed, no longer invisible but bound to a country that exists only in her keeping.
about_author: Lior Thornbury is the pen name of a former mountain rescue volunteer who spent six winters mapping disused trade routes across three countries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, belonging, and the people who live in the gaps between laws.

chapters.title: The Last Toll House
chapters.summary: Ines guides a salt caravan through a storm-closed pass, evading a Warden patrol, and returns to a guildhouse with only four members left. POV Ines. Beat: weary competence masking grief for a dying way of life.

chapters.title: A Knock in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: During the first snow, a barefoot child appears at the guild door speaking words Ines's mentor once called 'the language under all languages.' The matriarch, Sefa, goes pale. POV Ines. Beat: unease blooming into wonder—and dread.

chapters.title: What Sefa Buried
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the guild's true founding purpose: guarding knowledge of the Hollow Door. She recognizes the child's dialect as royal Vessarine. POV Sefa. Beat: guilt of long-kept secrets finally surfacing.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Ines seeks Tomas, a drunk ex-royal mapmaker whose family erased Vessar from every chart. He refuses—until he sees the child's birthmark. POV Tomas. Beat: shame transformed into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Gate
chapters.summary: Warden-Captain Aldric Vane arrives asking about 'an anomaly' reported on the mountain roads. Ines lies smoothly; the deserter Brann covers their tracks. POV Ines. Beat: first taste of real danger, sharpening her protective instinct.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Route
chapters.summary: Following her dead mentor's coded journal, Ines leads the group onto a smuggler's road that shouldn't exist. The child, named Nia by Sefa, begins speaking single words of common speech. POV Ines. Beat: hope kindling alongside fear.

chapters.title: Brann's Desertion
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Brann fled the Wardens after refusing to burn a village harboring 'old-blood' families. POV Brann. Beat: establishing his loyalty to Ines as redemption he doesn't believe he deserves.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: A hidden valley settlement greets Nia with reverence; elders sing a lullaby in Vessarine. Vane's scouts are closing in. POV Tomas. Beat: warmth of found community shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: One villager sells their location for amnesty. A skirmish at the river ford costs supplies and nearly takes Nia; Ines kills for the first time. POV Ines. Beat: innocence lost, duty hardening into something colder.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Captured briefly, Ines hears Vane's truth: he watched the Door's edge consume his brother. He offers her freedom if she surrenders the child. POV Vane. Beat: enemy humanized; the moral ground tilts.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Undermap
chapters.summary: Tomas navigates unmapped caverns using pre-Erasure charts. Brann holds a choke point alone and is gravely wounded. POV Tomas. Beat: terror and trust fused; the group becomes family in blood and stone.

chapters.title: Nia Speaks
chapters.summary: Sheltered in a shrine, Nia speaks full sentences: she remembers the sealing, remembers being chosen, remembers being afraid for two hundred years. POV Nia (rendered through Ines). Beat: heartbreak—the child is older than empires.

chapters.title: Sefa's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefa admits the guild once tried to open the Door generations ago and caused the winter that killed half the guild. Her guilt explains her secrecy. POV Sefa. Beat: forgiveness asked and imperfectly given.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Supernatural cold descends early and unnaturally—the Door weakening as Nia nears it. Villages freeze; refugees flood the passes. POV Ines. Beat: stakes become communal; invisibility is no longer possible or moral.

chapters.title: The Spire Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: The group reaches the Spire, Vessar's last visible tower, where the Door waits beneath. Vane's forces besiege the approach. POV Brann, from his sickbed directing them via signal mirror. Beat: defiance against impossible odds.

chapters.title: What Was Imprisoned
chapters.summary: Inside the Spire, they learn why Vessar was sealed: not tyranny, but a devouring thing wearing the king's face. Opening the Door risks freeing it. POV Tomas. Beat: revelation that reframes everything; despair sets in.

chapters.title: Vane's Assault
chapters.summary: Vane storms the Spire to collapse the Door with fire-oil. Brann dies holding the stair. Sefa takes a mortal wound shielding Nia. POV Brann then Ines. Beat: sacrifice upon sacrifice; rage and love indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Door
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Nia can reopen Vessar—but the devourer stirs. Vane, seeing his brother's fate echoed, wavers. Ines proposes the forbidden third option recorded in her mentor's journal. POV Ines. Beat: climax of decision; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Anchor
chapters.summary: Ines binds herself as the Door's living anchor, holding it closed from within while Nia lives free outside. Vane, broken, orders his Wardens home and burns his commission. POV Ines. Beat: the cost paid in full; transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: The Country in Her Keeping
chapters.summary: Ines, existing between, walks the preserved streets of sealed Vessar and confronts the devourer, holding it at bay with memory and will. POV Ines. Beat: solitary courage; the quiet war behind the door.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Months later, Nia—raised by Tomas and the valley village—visits the Spire. Through the Door's seam, Ines can speak a few words each thaw. The guild rebuilds around a new purpose. POV Nia. Beat: grief braided with continuity; found family endures.

chapters.title: Salt and Spire
chapters.summary: Years on, Nia as a young woman guides caravans along the old roads, teaching Vessarine songs. Each spring she brings salt to the Spire for Ines—an anchor needs anchoring too. POV Nia. Beat: resolution; love outlasting duty, a country kept alive in devotion.
